questions.question:
The classic two-branch recursion below returns what?
FUNCTION FIB(n)
IF n < 2 THEN RETURN n
RETURN FIB(n-1) + FIB(n-2)
END FUNCTION
PRINT FIB(6)
questions.explanation: Build the Fibonacci ladder from the base: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 — position 6 holds 8. Never expand the recursion tree in an exam; grow the sequence upward from 0, 1 and read off the answer.

questions.question:
What does the code output?

FOR i = 1 TO 10
IF i MOD 2 == 0 THEN CONTINUE
val = val + i
END FOR
PRINT val
questions.explanation: CONTINUE skips every multiple of 2, so the added values are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, totalling 25. CONTINUE abandons just the current pass; the loop itself marches on to the next i.
